amendment_2026_10_10.rule: The any-outside headline rule with the operand guard, as the advisor's 2026-10-14 review (ARCH-20261003-119, PART 2) ruled it. The 2026-10-10 review adopted the any-outside rule in place of the first quantity: an item holds only when every quantity the last results section that attributes the item's quantity collects under the unchanged attribution guards falls within the frozen key's tolerance, and the detail names the value that fails it. The 2026-10-14 ruling adds the operand guard that first form lacked: a derivation input is not a stated result, so a quantity that is an operand of arithmetic the answer shows is attributed to no item (the ruling's verbatim text is carried below, and in evals/tier2/versions.json's .3 entry). The guard repairs the first form's one defect - the recorded-correct regression vector 102-Q1, whose SECTION 7: SUMMARY OF RESULTS presents the divider's derivation in the Output Voltage row's Reference cell ('V_out = V_s × R2 / R_total = 12.0 V × 4.00 kΩ / 6.00 kΩ') beside the Value cell's 8.00 V, and whose unguarded rule collected the Reference cell's 12.0 V - a derivation input, the supply voltage the equation works on - as the Output voltage item's stated result, failing the vector 11/12 - and moves nothing else on the run's 71 delivered answers (the measurement below). The attribution guards are unchanged (a token distinctive to the item minus its same-dimension siblings' and none distinctive to a rival, function words never attributing, headings as section delimiters, parenthesized asides, bound words introducing requirements rather than values, the quantity converted to the key dimension's base unit). An answer that presents no results section that attributes the item's quantity is scored on its stated quantities as before - the rule tightens what a presented result counts for, it does not demand one.
amendment_2026_10_10.ruling_2026_10_14_verbatim: A derivation input is not a stated result. In the last results section that attributes the item's quantity, a quantity that is an operand of arithmetic the answer shows is attributed to no item. An operand is a number standing on either side of a binary operator: *, +, a spaced -, or ^ followed by a digit, sign or bracket. A slash divides between bare numbers written without spaces (210/17), or between quantities of different known dimensions (12.0 V / 6.00 k ohm). A slash between quantities of the same dimension, or where one side carries no unit, lists them (61.8 MPa / 176 MPa, 12.35 / 17.65 kN), and they stay stated values. The value an equation produces - the member after its last '=' - is stated unless an operator touches it. The degree sign's normalised '^ deg' is not an exponent, and an unspaced hyphen between numbers is a range, not a minus. Every other quantity is collected as before, under the unchanged attribution guards, and the item fails when any collected quantity lies outside the frozen key's tolerance.
amendment_2026_10_10.trigger: The advisor's 2026-10-14 review of the scorer branch (ARCH-20261003-119, PART 2), ruling on the contradiction the 2026-10-10 step-3 record reported (convention 18: the measurement was reported as it read, not adjusted): the ruled any-outside rule fails the recorded-correct regression vector 102-Q1 (11/12), because its last results section presents the divider's derivation in the Output Voltage row's Reference cell beside the Value cell's 8.00 V, and the unguarded rule collected the Reference cell's 12.0 V - a derivation input, not a stated result - as the Output voltage item's headline, failing the item on a figure the answer presents as an operand. The ruling: a derivation input is not a stated result. The ruled rule ships as frozen-2026-10-03.3 (PR #171, arch/20261008-scorer-recognition, rebased onto main 3526483 after the 2026-10-14 review's Part 1 merged); the .3 entry in evals/tier2/versions.json carries the ruling verbatim.
amendment_2026_10_10.the_operand_guard_vs_the_2026_10_10_draf: The advisor's probe, reproduced exactly. Across the 71 delivered answers, the operand guard moves exactly one item on one unit - C-Q23-r2's Common extension, FAIL to PASS (2/5 to 3/5 items), the unit's verdict unchanged FAIL. The extension's results table presents the derivation in its Reference cell: '| **Common extension ΔL** | **8.82×10⁻⁴ m (0.882 mm)** | 3/3400 m = 8.8235×10⁻⁴ m |'. Without the guard the bare-slash denominator 3400 m is collected as a stated quantity (far outside the 0.882353 mm key) and fails the item; with the guard the slash's operands are derivation inputs, the equation's product 8.8235×10⁻⁴ m (the member after its last '=') is stated, and the section's collected figures - the presented 0.882 mm and the derived 0.88235 mm - hold. No other unit's verdict or items move under the guard, so the review's condition - 'any move beyond C-Q23-r2's extension item: STOP and report' - is not met.

moves.reason: The answer's kill-trigger conditions state their limits as quantities: '(a) Linear elasticity. The request assumes it; no grades are supplied. Trigger: if the aluminum grade has 0.2 % proof strength below 93 MPa (= 1.5 × applied 61.8 MPa) or the steel has yield strength below 265 MPa (= 1.5 × applied 176 MPa)' and '6. PASS — Conditional assumptions carried with explicit kill triggers: elasticity void if Al proof < 93 MPa or steel yield < 265 MPa (1.5× applied)'. A comparison is not an operator, so 93 MPa and 265 MPa are stated values, not derivation inputs, and they attribute to the two tensile-stress items (their contexts name the materials); both lie far outside the keys' tolerances (61.8 ± 0.1 MPa, 176.5 ± 0.5 MPa), so the any-outside rule fails both items on them. Under the shipped first-quantity rule each stress item's headline was the presented in-tolerance figure (61.8 MPa, 176 MPa), so both held; the unit's verdict was already FAIL on the presented rounded forces (12.4/17.6 kN) and stays FAIL, with 1/5 items passing instead of 3/5. The operand guard does not repair this - '<' and 'below' are comparisons, not operators, and the ruling's letter keeps the limit figures stated; whether a kill-trigger limit should attribute to the item it bounds is a verdict-semantics question for the advisor, not a measurement defect - reported as it reads (convention 18).
